rex_01.text: A scruffy brown dog has been following you since Okuna. As you leave the outskirts he sits in the road ahead of you, tail wagging, blocking your path with cheerful obstinacy.

choices.text: "Alright. Come on then."
Give him some food and send him home.
Shoo him away. No place for a dog.
Kick the fleabag until it leaves you alone.

rex_joins.text: Rex leaps forward and falls into step beside you, tail still going. He immediately finds something dead to sniff.

rex_stays.text: Rex eats the food enthusiastically, watches you go, and sits down in the road. He will find his own way.

rex_dismissed.text: Rex watches you walk away with a look of profound, tail-drooping disappointment. You feel it between your shoulder blades for the next mile.

rex_abused.text: Rex yelps and scrambles away from you, all trust shattered in an instant. The sound lingers in the air long after he is gone.

stranger_01.text: A figure is slumped against a milestone at the side of the road. Alive — barely. A travelling merchant by the look of them, pack still on their back. They look up at you with exhausted eyes.

choices.text: Help them. Share food and water.
"What happened to you?"
Search their pack while they're too weak to stop you.
Keep walking. You cannot save everyone.

stranger_explains.text: "Bandits. Three of them, back on the Archer's Bend road. Took most of my coin. Left me the pack — said the goods weren't worth carrying." He coughs. "I'd give anything for water."

choices.text: Give them water and food.
"I'll watch out for those bandits. Good luck."

stranger_helped.text: "Bless you." He sits up straighter, colour returning. "I've nothing to give but this — there's a cave near Sapphire Lake, south side. Travelers have hidden supplies there. Most don't know about it."

stranger_robbed.text: The merchant is too weak to resist. He watches you go through his pack with dull, defeated eyes. "I thought—" he starts, then doesn't finish.

bandit_01.text: "End of the road, friend. Gold and food — leave it on the ground and walk away. We're not looking for trouble."

choices.text: Pay them off.
"You clearly don't know who I am."
Let your reputation speak for itself.
Offer food instead of gold.
Draw your weapon.

bandit_paid.text: He counts the gold, nods, and steps aside. "Pleasure doing business." The others laugh. You keep walking.

bandit_intimidated.text: He squints at you. Something clicks. His eyes widen slightly. "Let them through. Let them through." They step aside. Fast.

bandit_backs_down.text: The blood drains from his face. He's heard the name. He's heard the stories. "We don't want trouble," he says quietly. They melt back into the trees.

bandit_deal_food.text: He looks at the food, looks at you, and makes the practical decision. "Move on." A couple of the others look almost grateful.

dain_01.text: "You move like someone who knows where they're going but not what's ahead of them. I've walked the eastern road further than most. Where it gets... difficult." He pauses. "I could walk it again. With the right purpose."

choices.text: "Then walk with me."
"What would you want in return?"
"Tell me about the road ahead first."
Decline politely and move on.

dain_pitch.text: "Nothing beyond fair passage and honest purpose," he says. "I travel east in any case. Call it aligned interests."

choices.text: "Alright. Keep up."
"Still no."

dain_info.text: "The Badlands ahead are worse than the maps say. Two bridges are out. And something moves in the Brownback Wilds that is not bandits." He pauses. "That is free. My company costs more."

choices.text: "Fair enough. Come along."
"Good to know. I'll go alone."

dain_joins.text: "Then I walk with you." He falls into step, movements practiced and quiet. The party feels steadier already.

dain_refused.text: "The road is yours to walk as you choose." He returns to his post without looking back.

lefty_01.text: A lean man with quick eyes and a missing finger leans against a wall. "Heard about you. Word travels. You've made some interesting choices on the road." He finally looks at you. "Could use someone like you. Or you could use someone like me. Same thing, really."

choices.text: "What are you offering?"
"I don't trust anyone who opens with flattery."
Keep walking without acknowledging him.

lefty_pitch.text: "I know which merchants short-weigh, which innkeepers water the ale, and which guards can be... reasoned with. I'm good at finding things that aren't mine, and better at not getting caught." He smiles with half his mouth. "You're going somewhere dangerous. I've been there."

choices.text: "You're in. Try not to steal from me."
"I work alone."

lefty_pushback.text: He raises his hands. "Fair. No flattery then. You need someone who knows how to survive in places that want you dead. That's me. No pretty words about it."

choices.text: "Alright. Keep up."
"Still no."

lefty_joins.text: "Good call." He peels off the wall, pockets something you didn't see him pick up, and falls into step. "By the way — that innkeeper back there owes me three gold. We might want to leave quickly."

brannik_01.text: The old man doesn't look up from his fire. "Sit for a moment." It isn't a question. You sit.

brannik_02.text: "I've watched a hundred people walk this road. Some came back. Most didn't. You want to know the difference?" He pokes the fire. "The ones who came back weren't stronger. They weren't faster. They just didn't stop believing the road was going somewhere."

brannik_03.text: "Roachak knows you're coming. Has for a while. He's not afraid. That's his mistake." He goes back to his fire. "You should go. You've got what you came for."

coron_01.text: A gentle-faced priest in travel-worn robes stands at the wayside. "Peace be with you, traveler. The road is dark and filled with peril. May I offer you a blessing or heal your wounds?"

choices.text: "I require healing." (Costs 10 Gold)
"I seek your blessing."
"I seek your blessing."
"I need nothing. Farewell."

coron_healed.text: "May your body be restored for the journey ahead," he prays, placing his warm hands upon your brow. You feel a soothing light wash over you.

coron_blessed.text: "Your noble deeds on this road precede you," he smiles, tracing a sign of protection in the air. "Go with the light, traveler. You are blessed."

coron_refuse_blessing.text: He looks at you with sad eyes. "I sense conflict and dark rumors in your wake, traveler. I pray that you find your way back to the path of light, but I cannot offer a blessing today."

sylas_01.text: A sharp-looking man in fine silk coat stands beside a covered cart. "Ah, a fellow wanderer! I collect... rare curios. If you happen to have gold, I can sell you some maps, or I could buy any junk you found."

choices.text: "Sell me a treasure map." (Costs 15 Gold)
"I have some trinkets to sell."
"I must keep moving."

sylas_bought.text: He winks and hands you a dusty parchment map. "A fine choice! Let's hope it leads you to fortune, and not to your doom."

sylas_sold.text: He looks over your gear, nodding greedily, and hands you some gold coins. "A pleasure doing business with you, traveler. Let me know if you find more."

griselda_01.text: An old woman is crouching by a patch of wildflowers, humming quietly. She looks up with a pleasant smile. "Hello, traveler. Are you hungry, or do you have food to share with an old lady?"

choices.text: "Here is some of my food." (Lose 1 Food)
"Do you have any potions to sell?"
Nod politely and continue walking.

griselda_thankful.text: "Bless your kind soul!" she beams, taking the food. "Here, take this herbal poultice. It will soothe your burns and heal your spirits on the road."

griselda_sold.text: She reaches into her pocket and pulls out a small green bottle of herbal tincture. "Drink this when you are weary, it will restore your vigor."

finn_01.text: A young boy in dirty rags bumps hard into you as he runs past, muttering a quick apology before ducking into an alleyway.

choices.text: Confront him about your coin purse.
Pickpocket him back as he passes.
Ignore it and keep moving.

finn_caught.text: You grab his shoulder. He looks up in panic, showing a missing coin purse. "Alright, alright! Take it back! Don't call the guards!" He hands it over and scurries off.

finn_stole_back.text: With supreme stealth, you snatch his own pouch as he brushes past. Inside you find 10 gold. You feel a small thrill of thievish pride.

refugee_01.text: A family huddles beside a cart with a shattered wheel — a man, a woman, and two children, their belongings scattered across the verge. The woman looks up as you approach, exhaustion and wariness fighting for space on her face.

choices.text: Help repair the cart and share your supplies.
"What happened? Where are you headed?"
While they're distracted with the wheel, take what looks valuable.
Keep walking. You have your own road to worry about.

refugee_explains.text: "Soldiers came through our village three days back," he says, voice flat. "Said they were requisitioning for 'the war effort.' Took the grain stores, the livestock, half the roof timbers. We're making for anywhere with walls, honestly." He glances at his children. "Wheel snapped this morning. Bad luck on top of bad luck."

choices.text: Give them food and help with the wheel.
Wish them well and continue on your way.

refugee_helped.text: Between the two of you, the wheel is back on its axle within the hour. The woman presses a small bundle of dried herbs into your hands — "It isn't much, but it's all we have to give." The children watch you go with wide, grateful eyes.

refugee_robbed.text: You slip a few coins and a wrapped parcel of food from beneath the cart while the family struggles with the wheel. None of them notice — or if they do, none of them dare say anything. You walk on, the weight in your pack heavier than it should feel.

barn_01.text: Black smoke billows from a barn just off the road. Through the crackle of flame you hear it — a hoarse voice, shouting, and beneath it the panicked screams of trapped animals.

choices.text: Rush in and pull the person out.
Throw open the stalls and free the animals first.
Look for anyone else nearby before risking the fire.
The fire is too dangerous. Keep moving.

barn_search.text: You scan the surrounding fields. No one else is coming — whatever happens here, it's on you. The shouting from inside is growing weaker.

choices.text: Go in. There's no one else.
It isn't worth your life. Walk away.

barn_rescued.text: You wade through smoke and heat, dragging a coughing farmer out through the door moments before a beam crashes down behind you. He sags against you in the dirt, alive. "My family — I have to— thank you, thank you—" Word of what you did here will travel.

barn_animals.text: You wrench the stall doors open one by one. Goats and a terrified mule bolt past you into the open field, safe. The farmer staggers out moments later, soot-streaked, and watches his animals scatter across the grass. "You saved what you could," he rasps. "More than most would've stopped for."

traveler_01.text: A traveler approaches from the opposite direction — a merchant's apprentice, by the satchel slung across their shoulder. They slow as they near, clearly glad of company on the lonely road.

choices.text: Ask for news from the road ahead.
Share a meal and trade stories.
Nod and continue on without stopping.

traveler_news_node.text: "News? Prices are up something awful in the towns ahead — don't get fleeced. Roads get ugly after dark, more than usual lately. And folk keep talking about something stirring out east, though nobody seems to agree on what." They shrug. "Take it for what it's worth."

traveler_meal_node.text: You share a portion of your food, and in turn the apprentice presses a few coins into your palm. "Least I can do for the company," they say with a grin, before continuing on down the road, whistling.

outcast_01.text: Off the road, half-hidden in the brush, a lone figure sits with their back against a tree — tattered clothes, a crude brand scarred into one hand. They watch you with the wary stillness of someone used to being chased off.

choices.text: Approach slowly and offer some food.
Ask what happened to them.
They're alone and unguarded. Demand whatever coin they're carrying.
Keep your distance and move on.

outcast_story.text: "Branded a thief in my home village," they say, voice flat, like they've told it a hundred times. "For a crime I didn't commit. Wasn't worth fighting the verdict — easier to just... leave." They turn the marked hand over, studying it as if it belonged to someone else.

choices.text: "That's a hard thing to carry. Safe travels."
"Everyone has a story. Doesn't make it true."

outcast_grateful.text: They take the food without a word at first, turning it over in their hands like they don't quite believe it. Then, quietly: "...Thanks. Been a while since anyone bothered." They don't say anything else, but they watch you go without the wariness from before.

outcast_threatened.text: They flinch back against the tree, fumble a few coins from a hidden fold of cloth, and shove them at you with shaking hands, refusing to meet your eyes. You take the coins. Neither of you says anything.

rumor_01.text: The common room hums with low conversation. A weathered local at the next table leans toward you, lowering their voice.

choices.text: Lean in and listen.
You don't have time for gossip.

rumor_told.text: "Something's been stirring further down the road," they mutter. "Old stories, the kind nobody believed — until folk who went looking stopped coming back." They take a long drink and say nothing more. The warning settles in your gut, cold and certain.

mr1_01.text: A merchant with a heavily laden cart hails you from the roadside, eager to make one more sale before nightfall.

choices.text: Haggle hard for a better price.
Pay the asking price without complaint.
Decline and continue on your way.

mr1_done.text: "Pleasure doing business," the merchant says, wrapping a parcel of provisions and pressing it into your hands before snapping the reins and rattling off down the road.

mr2_01.text: "You there! Care for some news from the capital? Or—" she gestures at her cart "—I could always use a buyer for surplus grain."

choices.text: "What news do you have?"
Sell her some of your own surplus food.
"Not today."

mr2_news_node.text: "Prices on grain and salt are climbing in every town I've passed through. Folk are nervous about something — nobody quite says what." She shrugs, businesslike. "Bad for them, good for me, I suppose."

mr2_sell_node.text: She inspects your goods with a practiced eye, counts out coin without haggling, and tucks the food away among her own stores. "A fair trade. Safe travels."

mr3_01.text: A merchant's cart has thrown a wheel into a deep rut. He strains against the frame alone, cursing under his breath, his goods sliding dangerously toward the edge of the road.

choices.text: Help push the cart free.
Offer advice from a safe distance.
Keep walking. Not your cart, not your problem.

mr3_helped.text: Together you heave the wheel free of the rut. The merchant claps the dust from his hands, breathing hard, and digs a few coins out of his pouch. "Wouldn't have managed that alone. Much obliged, friend."

mr3_advice_node.text: "Helpful," he grunts, not looking up, as he wedges a branch under the axle and levers the cart free himself. "Real helpful." He doesn't thank you, but he doesn't curse you either, which you decide to count as a win.

sr1_01.text: A soldier sits hunched over a small fire just off the road, armor dented and travel-stained, staring into the flames as if they hold answers.

choices.text: Share a meal with them.
"Rough fight?"
Leave them to their thoughts.

sr1_share_node.text: They take the food without much ceremony, but something in their shoulders eases. "Been a while since anyone shared a fire without wanting something." You sit together a while, saying little, and it is enough.

sr1_ask_node.text: "Rough enough." They poke the fire with a stick. "Lost half my unit to something that came out of the dark and didn't look like it should be alive. Officers call it morale. I call it bad luck and worse maps." They fall silent again.

sr2_01.text: A soldier flags you down at a bend in the road. "Heads up — there's a checkpoint ahead, and they've been thorough lately. Just so you're not caught off guard."

choices.text: Thank them for the warning.
"Is there a way around it?"
Brush past — you don't answer to checkpoints.

sr2_thanks_node.text: "Don't mention it. Just keep your papers handy and you'll be through in no time." They give a tired nod and continue their own patrol.

sr2_around_node.text: They glance around before lowering their voice. "There's a track through the trees that skirts the checkpoint, but I didn't tell you that. Officially, I never saw you." They wink and wave you on.

sr3_01.text: A soldier limps along the road ahead of you, favoring one leg. As you draw closer you see a bandage at the thigh has soaked through, dark and fresh.

choices.text: Stop and help redress the wound.
Point them toward the next town.
Keep moving — it's not your concern.

sr3_help_node.text: You tear a strip of cloth and bind the wound properly, tight enough to slow the bleeding. The soldier grits their teeth through it, then exhales. "That's... actually a relief. Thank you. Truly."

sr3_point_node.text: "Town, right. That's the plan." They grimace and keep limping forward, jaw set, clearly intent on getting there under their own power no matter how long it takes.

rf1_01.text: A small family pauses on the road ahead, packs heavy on their backs. The eldest raises a hand in greeting. "Pardon — do you know if the road ahead is safe to the next town?"

choices.text: Share what you know of the road ahead.
"Just be careful," and continue on.
Walk past without answering.

rf1_share_node.text: You describe the route as best you can — where the road forks, where the footing turns bad. The family listens intently, nodding along. "Thank you, truly. Every bit helps."

rf1_caution_node.text: "Careful. Right." The family exchanges a tired look, gathers themselves, and presses on regardless — careful being a luxury they can't really afford to dwell on.

rf2_01.text: Evening finds a family camped just off the road, a small fire crackling. They wave you over. "Not much, but you're welcome to share what we have."

choices.text: Accept gladly, and add some of your own food to the pot.
Politely decline — you don't want to take their food.
Decline and continue down the road.

rf2_accept_node.text: The pooled meal stretches further than anyone expected, and for a little while the fire feels less like a refugee camp and more like something close to home. You sleep a little easier that night.

rf2_polite_node.text: "Suit yourself," they say, not unkindly, and budge over to make room at the fire anyway. You warm yourself for a few minutes before continuing on, glad of the brief respite.

rf3_01.text: A worried-looking woman hurries toward you. "Please — have you seen a boy on the road, about ten years old, brown coat? We got separated when the crowd at the crossing scattered."

choices.text: Promise to keep an eye out for him.
Tell her you haven't, and wish her luck.
You don't have time for this.

rf3_promise_node.text: "Bless you. Brown coat, dark hair, answers to Tomas." She presses on past you, calling his name into the trees, voice already hoarse from calling it for hours.

rf3_no_node.text: Her face falls, just slightly, before she steadies herself. "No. Right. Thank you anyway." She hurries on down the road, calling a name into the wind.

hr1_01.text: An old hermit sits cross-legged beside a small cairn of stones, eyes closed, lips moving in some private litany. They do not seem to notice you at first.

choices.text: Ask for their wisdom.
Leave an offering of food by the cairn.
Walk past quietly and leave them undisturbed.

hr1_ask_node.text: One eye opens. "Wisdom." They consider this. "The road behind you is fixed. The road ahead is not. Most people have that backwards." The eye closes again. You wait, but nothing more comes.

hr1_offer_node.text: Without opening their eyes, the hermit inclines their head a fraction. "The cairn remembers kindness, even if the hands that gave it are long gone." It is, you decide, as close to a thank-you as you are likely to get — and somehow it is enough.

hr2_01.text: The hermit's hand shoots out and grips your sleeve as you pass. "Wait. The birds went quiet an hour ago and haven't started again. That's not nothing. Mind how you go today."

choices.text: Thank them and heed the warning.
Laugh it off — birds are birds.
Pull your sleeve free and keep walking.

hr2_heed_node.text: The hermit releases your sleeve, satisfied. "Good. Eyes open, then." They settle back against the cairn, already returning to whatever private vigil you interrupted. You walk on a little more watchful than before.

hr2_laugh_node.text: "Laugh if you like." The hermit shrugs, entirely unbothered. "The birds won't mind either way." You continue on, still chuckling — though you find yourself listening for birdsong all the same.

hr3_01.text: The hermit holds out an open palm, weathered and steady. "A blessing, for a bit of food. Old magic, older roads. Costs you little, and it might just keep the worst of the dark off your back."

choices.text: Accept the trade.
Politely decline.
Scoff at the idea of "old magic."

hr3_accept_node.text: The hermit takes the food and presses two fingers briefly to your forehead, murmuring something in a language you don't recognize. The words fade, but the warmth of them lingers a moment, and you feel — strangely — a little lighter for the road ahead.

hr3_mock_node.text: The hermit's outstretched hand withdraws without complaint. "As you like." They close their eyes again, and somehow the silence that follows feels colder than it should.

br1_01.text: A bard sits beneath a roadside tree, lute across one knee, voice raised in an old traveling song. They catch your eye and give a little flourish, an open invitation.

choices.text: Toss a coin and stay to listen.
Ask for a song, coinless.
Walk on without stopping.

br1_tip_node.text: The coin lands in their open case with a satisfying clink, and the bard rewards you with a grin and a song that swells louder, brighter — the kind of tune that makes tired feet feel a little less tired.

br1_free_node.text: The bard raises an eyebrow but plays anyway — a shorter tune, noticeably less enthusiastic, ending with a pointed look at their empty case as you walk away.

br2_01.text: "You've the look of someone with stories to tell," the bard says, tuning a string. "Care to share one? Good material is hard to come by, and a good story has a way of... traveling."

choices.text: Share a true story from your travels.
Exaggerate wildly for effect.
You're not in a storytelling mood.

br2_true_node.text: The bard listens with genuine interest, occasionally humming a phrase as if testing how it might fit a melody. "That's good. That's real good. Don't be surprised if you hear your own name sung back to you in some tavern down the road."

br2_exaggerate_node.text: By the time you finish, the bard is grinning ear to ear, scribbling furiously on a scrap of parchment. "A *dragon*, you said? Wonderful. Absolutely none of that happened, did it. I love it. Keep going."

br3_01.text: Between songs, the bard leans on their lute and lowers their voice conspiratorially. "Word of advice — the innkeeper two towns over waters down the ale somethin' fierce. And the toll collector before that? Took a bribe from a fella who turned out to be wanted in three counties. Free entertainment, that."

choices.text: Listen to the gossip.
Tip them for the information.
Move along.

br3_listen_node.text: The bard happily rattles off a string of small-town scandals, half of which are probably true. None of it changes your plans, but it's good to know which doors might open a little easier with the right name dropped.

br3_tip_node.text: The bard pockets the coin with a wink and leans in even closer, dropping their voice further still — as if the gossip were somehow worth more now that money has changed hands. It mostly isn't, but you appreciate the showmanship.

st1_01.text: A hooded figure stands motionless at the far side of the road, watching you. They make no move to approach — but they make no move to leave, either.

choices.text: Approach and ask what they want.
Try to lift their coin purse as you pass.
Keep walking, eyes forward.

st1_confront_node.text: You cross the road, squaring your shoulders. The figure flinches back a step, mutters something that might be an apology, and hurries off into the trees without a backward glance. Whatever they wanted, it apparently wasn't worth a confrontation.

st1_pickpocket_node.text: A practiced brush of the shoulder as you pass, and their purse is suddenly in your sleeve. By the time they notice the weight is gone, you're well down the road — though you can't shake the feeling those eyes are still on you.

st2_01.text: A figure falls into step beside you, voice pitched low. "I know things. Things worth knowing, for the right traveler. For a small fee, of course."

choices.text: Pay for the information.
Refuse and step away.
Make it clear they should talk for free.

st2_pay_node.text: The coin disappears into their sleeve. "Smart traveler keeps to well-lit roads after dark, this season." That's it — that's the whole of it. Vague, unsettling, and somehow worth exactly what you paid for it.

st2_threaten_node.text: They go very still, then laugh — a thin, humorless sound. "Fine, fine. Free advice: don't threaten people who know things about you that you don't know they know." They vanish into the crowd before you can press further, leaving you faintly unsettled.

st3_01.text: You've had the prickling sense of being followed for the better part of an hour. Glancing back confirms it — a cloaked figure, keeping pace, not bothering to hide anymore now that you've noticed.

choices.text: Turn and confront them directly.
Duck off the road and lose them.
Ignore it and hope they lose interest.

st3_confront_node.text: You spin to face them, hand drifting to your weapon. The figure freezes, then turns and bolts back the way they came, robes flapping, vanishing around a bend before you can get a good look at their face.

st3_lose_node.text: You slip behind a stand of trees and wait, breath held. Footsteps approach, slow, then pass — and a moment later, an irritated curse drifts back as your follower realizes the road ahead is empty. You wait a while longer before continuing, just to be sure.

pl1_01.text: A robed pilgrim walks the road ahead of you at a steady, unhurried pace, prayer beads clicking softly through their fingers with each step.

choices.text: Match their pace and walk together a while.
Ask where they are headed, and why.
Continue at your own pace.

pl1_walk_node.text: Neither of you says much, but the company is its own kind of comfort. After a mile or so, the pilgrim murmurs a soft blessing over the road ahead — for both of you, it seems — before falling back into quiet contemplation.

pl1_ask_node.text: "There is a shrine, some days from here, said to grant clarity to those who reach it with an honest heart." They smile faintly. "I have walked a long way already. A little further costs nothing."

pl2_01.text: The pilgrim pauses at a roadside shrine, weathered by years of rain, and glances at you. "Would you like a moment of prayer for your journey? It costs nothing, and the road is long."

choices.text: Accept the prayer.
Politely decline — it's not your faith.
Scoff at the offer.

pl2_accept_node.text: They speak a few quiet words over the worn stone, hand resting briefly on your shoulder. It is a small thing — and yet you find yourself standing a little straighter as you continue down the road.

pl2_decline_node.text: "As you wish — the offer costs nothing to make, and nothing to decline." They say their own prayer quietly, alone, and you wait respectfully a moment before continuing on together.

pl2_scoff_node.text: The pilgrim doesn't rise to it. "Faith asks nothing of those who lack it," they say mildly, and turn back to the shrine, leaving you to feel slightly more churlish than you intended.

pl3_01.text: The pilgrim stops mid-stride and studies you for a long moment, head tilted, as though weighing something only they can see.

choices.text: Hold their gaze and wait.
Hold their gaze and wait.
Nod and continue past.

pl3_blessed_node.text: The pilgrim's expression softens into something like reverence. "A light walks with you," they murmur, bowing their head briefly before continuing on their way. You're not sure what they saw, but it felt like a gift.

pl3_concerned_node.text: Their eyes narrow, and they take a half-step back. "Walk carefully," they say, voice quieter than before. "Shadows cling to you, traveler — whether you asked for them or not." They hurry on without another word.

sc1_01.text: A scout leans against a roadside tree, leg bound in a crude, blood-soaked bandage, a map case still strapped tight across their back despite everything.

choices.text: Stop and help tend the wound properly.
Ask what happened.
Leave them be.

sc1_help_node.text: You clean and rebind the wound with what you can spare. The scout hisses through their teeth but holds still, watching you work with grudging respect. "Didn't expect that. Most people just keep walking. Thanks."

sc1_ask_node.text: "Got too close to something I shouldn't have, scouting the ridgeline back there." They jerk a thumb vaguely behind them. "Made it out. Mostly. Not in a hurry to go back, I'll tell you that much."

sc2_01.text: A scout has a battered map spread across their knees, marking it with quick, practiced strokes. "Got the safer routes through this stretch marked, if you're interested. Trade you for some food — scouting on an empty stomach is miserable work."

choices.text: Trade food for the route information.
Just ask for directions, no trade.
Not interested.

sc2_trade_node.text: They eat gratefully while talking you through the safest paths ahead — where the ground holds, where it doesn't, where the going is slow but secure. It's the kind of knowledge that's hard to put a price on, and you got it for the cost of a meal.

sc2_ask_node.text: They give you a flat look — but answer anyway, albeit more briefly than they might have otherwise. "Stick to the high ground past the river bend. That's the free version." They go back to their map without further comment.

sc3_01.text: A scout jogs up the road toward you, breathing hard. "Careful up ahead — spotted movement off the road, more than one. Could be nothing. Could be a problem. Wanted to give you the warning either way."

choices.text: Thank them and stay alert.
Ask for more details.
You can handle yourself.

sc3_thanks_node.text: "Smart. Better cautious than caught off guard." They give you a quick nod and continue down the road at the same urgent pace, off to deliver the same warning to anyone else they pass.

sc3_details_node.text: "Three, maybe four. Moving in a loose line, not a patrol formation — could be travelers, could be something else entirely. Didn't stick around to find out which." They shrug helplessly. "Wish I had more for you."

sc3_shrug_node.text: "Sure. Your call." The scout doesn't argue further, just moves on with a faintly worried backward glance — the kind of look that lingers a little longer in your mind than you'd like to admit.

nb1_01.text: A finely dressed noble passes in a small carriage with a modest guard escort, nose wrinkled at the state of the road — and, briefly, at the state of you.

choices.text: Bow respectfully as they pass.
Ignore them entirely.
Make a cutting remark about their escort's posture.

nb1_bow_node.text: The noble offers the barest acknowledgment — a single curt nod, as if granting you a great favor by noticing you at all — before the carriage rattles on without further ceremony.

nb1_remark_node.text: The guard in question goes red; the noble goes redder. The carriage picks up speed noticeably as it passes, and you walk on feeling rather pleased with yourself, reputation among the nobility notwithstanding.

nb2_01.text: A noble's carriage sits at an awkward angle, a wheel pin fallen loose in the mud. The guards stand around looking uncomfortable, clearly unwilling to dirty their fine gloves.

choices.text: Offer to fix it yourself.
Direct them to the nearest town for help.
Enjoy the spectacle and move on.

nb2_fix_node.text: You find the missing pin in the mud and hammer it back into place with a rock. The noble watches from inside the carriage the entire time, then tosses out a small pouch of coin without quite making eye contact. "For your trouble," they say, in a tone that suggests it was, in fact, beneath them.

nb2_direct_node.text: You point out the town visible on the horizon and continue on your way. Behind you, the noble begins loudly instructing a guard to walk there and bring back a wheelwright — a journey that guard does not look forward to in the slightest.

nb3_01.text: A noble traveler eyes your worn gear as you pass and remarks, just loudly enough to be heard, "I do wonder why such rough sorts are permitted on the main roads at all."

choices.text: Let the insult slide.
Respond with cutting wit.
Step menacingly closer until they reconsider.

nb3_wit_node.text: "Funny," you reply, "I was just thinking the same about people who travel with three guards because they're afraid of a road." The noble splutters; their guards very visibly try not to smile. You walk on, thoroughly satisfied.

nb3_step_node.text: You take one slow step toward them. The noble's composure evaporates entirely, and they practically scramble back into their carriage, shouting at the driver to move along immediately. The guards exchange a look but don't intervene.

ds1_01.text: A man in a torn, unmarked uniform startles badly at your approach, hand flying to an empty scabbard at his hip before he catches himself. He looks like he hasn't slept in days.

choices.text: Tell him you mean no harm.
Ask why he ran.
Remind him deserters are hanged — maybe someone should know where he is.

ds1_calm_node.text: His shoulders drop, just slightly. "Sorry. Sorry — you just... you can't be too careful." He doesn't explain further, but the wariness in his eyes eases, just a fraction, and he nods you past without further trouble.

ds1_ask_node.text: "Why does anyone run." It isn't really a question. "Saw enough. Did enough. Couldn't do any more of it." He won't meet your eyes, but he doesn't seem dangerous — just hollowed out, and very far from wherever home used to be.

ds1_threaten_node.text: All the color drains from his face. Without a word, he turns and bolts into the underbrush, crashing through branches in his haste to be anywhere but here. You feel a brief, ugly satisfaction — followed quickly by something closer to shame.

ds2_01.text: The deserter falls into step a short distance away, keeping his eyes on the road. "I know things — troop movements, patrol schedules. Worth something to the right person. I just need enough food to keep moving. Please."

choices.text: Give him food and let him go, no questions.
Take the information but give nothing in return.
Walk away — not your problem.

ds2_give_node.text: He takes the food with both hands, like it might be snatched away. "You didn't have to—" he starts, then just nods instead, throat working. "Thank you. Really." He's gone before you can say anything else.

ds2_take_node.text: Hope flickers across his face as he talks — patrol routes, changing of the guard, all of it tumbling out in a rush. When he finishes and looks at you expectantly, you simply walk on. His expression crumples, but he doesn't follow.

ds3_01.text: A gaunt figure steps out from behind a roadside boulder, a rusted knife shaking visibly in his grip. "I — I just need supplies. Don't make this hard. Please don't make this hard."

choices.text: Hand over a little food to defuse the situation.
Stand your ground — he's too scared to follow through.
Step in close and twist the knife from his grip.

ds3_give_node.text: He grabs the food and stumbles back immediately, knife clattering forgotten to the ground. "I'm sorry — I'm so sorry—" He's already running before he finishes the sentence, leaving the knife behind in the dirt.

ds3_stand_node.text: You don't move, don't flinch. The knife trembles harder in his grip — and then his nerve breaks entirely. He turns and flees empty-handed, leaving only the echo of his ragged breathing behind.

ds3_disarm_node.text: Before he can react, you step inside his guard and twist the knife free in one motion. He collapses against the boulder, sobbing with something that might be relief as much as fear. You toss the rusted blade into the brush and walk on, leaving him to gather himself.

gd1_01.text: A guard at a small roadside post waves you down. "Routine check, won't take but a moment. Just need to see what you're carrying."

choices.text: Cooperate fully.
Make idle conversation while they check.
Sigh loudly and act put out by the delay.

gd1_cooperate_node.text: The guard gives your pack a cursory glance, nods, and waves you through without further comment. The whole thing takes less time than it took to stop walking.

gd1_chat_node.text: The guard, clearly bored out of their mind, brightens considerably and chats amiably while poking through your pack — mostly about how slow the day has been. You part on friendlier terms than most travelers manage here.

gd1_annoyed_node.text: The guard's expression flattens, and the "routine" check becomes noticeably more thorough — every pocket, every fold of cloth — purely, you suspect, out of spite. Eventually they wave you through, unsmiling.

gd2_01.text: A guard leaning against a post calls out as you pass. "Heads up — there's a curfew in the next town after dark. Patrols have been jumpy lately. Wouldn't want you caught out after hours."

choices.text: Thank them for the heads up.
Ask what's caused the trouble.
Brush it off.

gd2_thanks_node.text: "No trouble. Just trying to keep folk from getting an arrow in the dark over a misunderstanding." They give a small wave and settle back against their post as you continue on.

gd2_why_node.text: "Couple of break-ins, some unrest down by the market square. Nothing official, but the captain doesn't like surprises after dark, and neither do I." They shrug. "Just plan your evening accordingly, that's all."

gd3_01.text: A guard blocks the road with a lazy gesture. "Road maintenance fee. New policy." There is, you note, no sign, no ledger, and no other guards anywhere nearby collecting any such fee.

choices.text: Pay up to avoid the hassle.
Refuse and demand to see their superior.
Walk past without acknowledging the "fee."

gd3_pay_node.text: The coin disappears into a pocket with practiced speed, and the guard steps aside with a thin smile. "Pleasure doing business. Safe travels." Neither of you mentions the word "bribe," which somehow makes it worse.

gd3_refuse_node.text: The guard's confident smirk falters. "...Right. Course. Just, ah — just doing my rounds, then." They step aside hastily, suddenly very interested in something on the horizon. A small crowd of onlookers nearby seem quietly pleased.

hl1_01.text: A traveler with a satchel of jars and bundled herbs slung across their back smiles as you approach. "You look like you've been on the road a while. Care for a quick checkup? No charge — practice keeps the hands sharp."

choices.text: Accept the offer.
Politely decline — you're fine.
Ask for a remedy in trade for a few coins.

hl1_accept_node.text: Quick, practiced hands check your pulse, your eyes, the set of your shoulders. "Tired, but sound," they pronounce, and press a small poultice into your palm regardless. "Keep that on anything that aches tonight. On the house."

hl1_trade_node.text: They mix a small vial from their satchel — bitter-smelling, but it settles warm in your stomach and eases the ache in your legs almost immediately. "Good for the road," they say, pocketing the coins with a satisfied nod.

hl2_01.text: You find the healer crouched at the roadside, carefully sorting through a patch of low-growing plants. "Ah — good timing, actually. I'm hunting for a particular root that grows along verges like this. Care to help me look? Won't take long."

choices.text: Help search through the underbrush.
Point out a patch you noticed earlier.
Decline — you wouldn't know what to look for.

hl2_help_node.text: Between the two of you, the right roots turn up before long. The healer beams and presses a small bundled remedy into your hands. "For your trouble — and your patience with an old habit of mine. Keep it; you never know."

hl2_remedy.text: The remedy proves immediately useful — applied to a half-healed scrape, it numbs the ache almost instantly.

hl2_point_node.text: "Oh — yes, that'll do nicely, thank you!" They hurry off toward the patch you indicated, already murmuring happily to themselves about root quality. A small thing, but it clearly made their day.

hl3_01.text: The healer sits on a milestone, satchel mostly empty beside them. "Slow season," they admit when you pass. "Folk don't spare much for remedies when they're short on food themselves. Can't blame them, really."

choices.text: Give them a few coins.
Offer sympathy, nothing more.
Suggest they charge more for their work.

hl3_give_node.text: They stare at the coins in their palm for a moment before closing their fingers around them. "That's — thank you. Truly." Their eyes are a little brighter as they tuck the coins away and gather their things with renewed energy.

hl3_sympathy_node.text: "It'll turn around. It always does, eventually." They say it more for their own benefit than yours, by the sound of it, but they seem to appreciate having someone to say it to.

hl3_suggest_node.text: They let out a tired laugh. "Charge more, and watch everyone walk straight past me to the next healer down the road. No — better to make less and actually help someone, I think." They don't seem to regret the choice, even now.

cv1_01.text: A small merchant caravan rumbles past — three wagons, well-guarded, piled with goods under canvas. The lead driver calls out, "Provisions, if you need them! Won't find better prices between here and the next town!"

choices.text: Buy some travel provisions.
Ask where they are headed.
Wave them on without stopping.

cv1_buy_node.text: The driver tosses down a sack of provisions without even slowing the wagon much, catching your coins in the same motion. "Pleasure! Mind the road ahead, it's a bit rough past the bend!" And then they're gone in a cloud of dust.

cv1_ask_node.text: "Markets further down the road — good prices on grain this season, or so we're hoping!" The driver grins, clearly an optimist by trade as much as nature, and the caravan continues on without losing momentum.

cv2_01.text: A caravan guard flags you down as their wagons roll to a brief halt. "Word of warning — bandits hit a caravan not far from here, two days back. Lost goods, nobody hurt, but they're still out there somewhere. Travel careful."

choices.text: Thank them and stay alert.
Offer to scout ahead for trouble.
Tell them you can handle a few bandits.

cv2_thanks_node.text: "Smart. Eyes open, that's all anyone can do out here." The guard nods and climbs back aboard the wagon as the caravan creaks back into motion, wheels grinding against the gravel.

cv2_scout_node.text: You move ahead a short distance, checking the treeline and the bends in the road, before waving the caravan onward. "Appreciate it, truly," the guard calls as they pass — a small thing, but it clearly eased a few nerves.

cv2_handle_node.text: The guard raises an eyebrow but doesn't argue. "Confidence. I like that." They climb back aboard, and the caravan trundles off — whether reassured or just amused by you, it's hard to say.

cv3_01.text: The caravan master slows their wagon alongside you. "Heading the same direction, looks like. Roads are safer in numbers, if you don't mind the pace of a wagon train. You're welcome to walk with us a stretch."

choices.text: Accept gladly.
Decline — you'll move faster alone.
Accept, but keep a hand near your coin purse.

cv3_accept_node.text: The next stretch of road passes easily in the company of the caravan — idle conversation, shared rations, the rhythmic creak of wagon wheels. When your paths finally diverge, the master tips their hat warmly. "Good company. Safe travels, friend."

cv3_guard_node.text: You walk alongside the caravan, friendly enough but watchful — old habits. Nothing untoward happens, of course, and by the time you part ways you almost feel a little silly for the precaution. Almost.

ch1_01.text: A small child sits at the edge of the road, knees pulled up to their chest, crying quietly. There's no one else in sight in any direction.

choices.text: Stop and help them find their family.
Ask what happened.
You can't help everyone — keep moving.

ch1_help_node.text: You crouch down, speak gently, and after a few false starts the child manages to point out a path off the main road — "we were picking berries and I just... I couldn't see them anymore." It doesn't take long to find the frantic family nearby; their relief is immediate and overwhelming.

ch1_ask_node.text: "We were picking berries and I — I couldn't find anyone anymore," the child hiccups. You help them retrace their steps along a side path, and within minutes a relieved voice calls out from among the trees. The reunion is brief, tearful, and entirely worth the detour.

ch2_01.text: A child sitting on a fence post calls out as you pass. "Hey! I know a secret shortcut through the woods! I'll tell you for one coin!" They look extremely pleased with this business plan.

choices.text: Pay for the tip.
Decline politely.
Ask if they'll tell you for free.

ch2_pay_node.text: The child pockets the coin with great solemnity, then leans in conspiratorially. "Okay, so — if you go past the big rock, and then past the OTHER big rock, there's a path! Probably!" You're fairly sure this is not, in fact, a real shortcut. It was worth every coin anyway.

ch2_free_node.text: The child considers this with great seriousness, then shakes their head firmly. "Nope! Information costs money. That's how it works." They cross their arms, utterly immovable on this point of principle.

ch3_01.text: A child runs up alongside you, holding both fists out. "Guess which hand! If you win, you're really smart. If you lose, you have to admit I'm smarter. Those are the rules."

choices.text: Play along.
No time for games.
Play, and let them win on purpose.

ch3_play_node.text: You guess wrong — both hands turn out to be empty, which the child finds absolutely hilarious. "You have to admit I'm smarter now! Those are the rules!" You admit it. They run off thoroughly delighted with themselves.

ch3_lose_node.text: You guess "wrong" with theatrical dismay, and the child positively glows with triumph, declaring themselves the smartest person on the entire road, possibly in the whole region. They skip off in great spirits, and somehow so do you.

rex_ci_01.text: Rex trots up and drops something at your feet with enormous pride — a stick, by the look of it, though it's hard to be sure after however many times he's chewed on it.

choices.text: Take the stick and give it a proper throw.
Admire it like the rare treasure he believes it to be.
Step over it and keep walking.

rex_ci_throw_node.text: Rex tears off after it with the single-minded joy of a creature who has never once considered that this might be a trick. He brings it back. He will bring it back again. And again.

rex_ci_admire_node.text: You turn the stick over with great solemnity, as though appraising fine craftsmanship. Rex's tail nearly knocks you off balance.

rex_b_01.text: Rex is still riding the high of the fight, circling you at a trot and occasionally barking at nothing in particular, as if reliving the highlights.

choices.text: Ruffle his fur — he did good.
Tell him to settle down — eyes on the road.
Let him sniff around the aftermath.

rex_b_ruffle_node.text: He leans into your hand, tongue lolling, entirely too pleased with himself — and, frankly, he earned it.

rex_b_settle_node.text: He quiets, mostly, though his ears stay pricked and alert for several minutes afterward — a habit that's saved you both more than once.

rex_b_sniff_node.text: He noses through the scene with great purpose, learns nothing of obvious value, and seems entirely satisfied with that outcome regardless.

rex_s_01.text: Rex is still drying out from the storm, fur standing up in damp clumps, and he presses himself against your leg with the full weight of his unhappiness.

choices.text: Towel him off properly with a spare cloth.
Give him a brisk, undignified rubdown.
He'll dry on his own eventually.

rex_s_towel_node.text: He stands very still for it, which for Rex is practically a religious experience, and emerges looking marginally more dignified and considerably warmer.

rex_s_rub_node.text: He shakes indignantly halfway through, spraying water everywhere, then flops down looking thoroughly betrayed but somewhat drier.

rex_d_01.text: Rex doesn't bound up the way he usually does. Instead he sits a short distance away, ears low, watching you with the particular stillness of a dog who has noticed something is wrong.

choices.text: Sit down with him for a moment.
Give him a reassuring pat and keep moving.
Tell him to knock it off — not now.

rex_d_sit_node.text: He shuffles closer and rests his head on your knee, and for a few minutes neither of you needs to be anywhere else. It helps more than you expected.

rex_d_pat_node.text: He leans into the touch briefly before falling back into step beside you — not fixed, exactly, but a little steadier.

rex_r_01.text: Rex's nose goes into overdrive as you pass through the country near Okuna — old scents, old ground. He keeps glancing back the way you came, then trotting to catch up.

choices.text: Wonder if he misses it.
Tell him this is home now, wherever you're walking.
Keep walking — he'll catch up.

rex_r_miss_node.text: If he does, he doesn't show it for long — by the time you've gone another mile, his attention's already three smells ahead of you, same as always.

rex_r_home_node.text: He looks up at you for a long moment, then presses against your leg once, hard, before trotting on ahead — tail up, leading the way like he always does.

emmy_ci_01.text: Emmy is crouched over her satchel, sorting dried herbs into neat little bundles by feel as much as sight. "How are you holding up? Honestly, not the polite answer."

choices.text: Tell her honestly how you're feeling.
Say you're fine and change the subject.
Ask if she has anything for "general weariness of the soul."

emmy_ci_honest_node.text: She listens without interrupting, nods once when you finish, and tucks a small dried sprig into your pack without comment. "For later. No charge."

emmy_ci_fine_node.text: "Mm," she says, in a tone that makes it clear she doesn't believe you for a second — but she lets it go, and goes back to her herbs.

emmy_ci_joke_node.text: "Afraid not — that one's chronic." She allows herself the ghost of a smile before returning to her sorting.

emmy_b_01.text: Emmy checks you over with quick, practiced hands before you've even fully caught your breath, muttering half to herself about scrapes that "will need watching."

choices.text: Thank her for the fast work.
Ask how she stays so calm in a fight.
Wave off the fuss — you're fine.

emmy_b_thanks_node.text: "Don't thank me yet — thank me if none of this gets infected." But there's warmth under the brisk tone, and she finishes binding the worst of it without further argument.

emmy_b_calm_node.text: "Practice. And the alternative is panicking, which has never once stitched a wound." She ties off the bandage with a small, decisive tug.

emmy_b_wave_node.text: "You're fine until you're not," she says, unmoved, and finishes checking your arm anyway. You let her. It's easier that way.

emmy_s_01.text: Emmy spends a long while after the storm carefully unwrapping oilcloth from her satchel, checking each bundle of herbs for water damage with visible relief when most have survived.

choices.text: Ask how bad it would have been if they'd spoiled.
Offer to help her re-wrap everything properly.
Leave her to it.

emmy_s_ask_node.text: "Weeks of gathering, gone in an afternoon. It's happened before." She says it lightly, but you notice she double-wraps everything afterward, just in case.

emmy_s_help_node.text: Between the two of you it goes quickly, and she seems genuinely grateful for the extra hands — and, perhaps, the company while doing something so methodical.

emmy_d_01.text: Emmy doesn't say anything for a while, just walks beside you with her satchel held a little tighter than usual. Eventually: "I keep thinking about how much further there is to go. And whether what we're carrying will be enough."

choices.text: Tell her you'll figure it out together.
Admit you're worried too, but keep moving.
Tell her not to worry — you'll find more supplies on the way.

emmy_d_together_node.text: She glances at you, surprised, then nods slowly. "Together. Right." It's a small thing, but her shoulders ease a little, and she walks a bit lighter for the rest of the day.

emmy_d_admit_node.text: "At least it's not just me, then," she says, with something like relief, and the two of you walk on without needing to say much else.

emmy_d_reassure_node.text: She gives you a long, level look — the kind that suggests she's heard that particular promise before, from people who didn't keep it. But she doesn't argue.

emmy_r_01.text: Emmy slows as the road curves toward familiar country. "Lahonis isn't far from here. I learned most of what I know about herbs from an old woman in that market — sharpest tongue I ever met, and the gentlest hands."

choices.text: Ask if you'll pass close enough to visit.
Suggest making time to stop, if she'd like.
Note that the road doesn't really allow for detours.

emmy_r_visit_node.text: "Maybe close enough to see the rooftops. That'll have to do, I think." She says it without much disappointment — more like setting something down gently.

emmy_r_stop_node.text: She seems caught off guard by the offer, then shakes her head, smiling faintly. "Another time, maybe. But — thank you for asking."

emmy_r_no_node.text: "No, I know," she says, and that's the end of it — though she watches the horizon a little longer than usual before turning back to the road ahead.

dain_ci_01.text: Dain sits apart from the others, running a whetstone along his blade in slow, even strokes — a ritual more than a necessity, by the look of the edge already.

choices.text: Ask what he's thinking about.
Sit with him in companionable silence.
Ask if the blade is offended by how much attention it gets.

dain_ci_ask_node.text: Dain pauses. "The road behind. The road ahead. Which parts of each I'd rather forget." He doesn't elaborate, but doesn't seem to mind the question either.

dain_ci_silence_node.text: He nods once, acknowledging you, and the two of you sit without speaking until the stone's rhythm becomes its own kind of conversation.

dain_ci_joke_node.text: A long pause. "It has never complained." He doesn't smile, but something in his eyes suggests he might be enjoying this slightly more than he lets on.

dain_b_01.text: Dain cleans his blade with the same unhurried care he gives everything, eyes fixed on some middle distance. "Clean kills. No wasted motion. You're learning."

choices.text: Tell him you're trying to live up to that standard.
Ask what "wasted motion" means to a warrior like him.
Just nod and move on.

dain_b_aspire_node.text: He studies you for a moment, then gives the smallest of nods — from Dain, this is practically a parade.

dain_b_ask_node.text: "Fear. Anger. Both make you slower, not faster, whatever the songs say. Strip those away, and what's left is just... the work."

dain_b_nod_node.text: He returns to his blade without further comment, which from Dain is its own kind of approval.

dain_s_01.text: Dain stands at the edge of camp long after the storm passes, watching the clouds break apart over the horizon, seemingly unbothered by how soaked through he still is.

choices.text: Ask if storms like that bother the Qanisi.
Suggest he get out of the wet clothes before he catches a chill.
Comment that he looks like he's carved from the same stone as the cliffs.

dain_s_ask_node.text: "The mountains where I trained see worse, more often. This—" he gestures at the dripping camp "—is a light afternoon."

dain_s_dry_node.text: He glances down at himself as if noticing for the first time, then allows, "...A reasonable point," before finally moving toward dry ground.

dain_s_remark_node.text: He doesn't quite smile, but something near it crosses his face. "I've been called worse."

dain_d_01.text: Dain falls into step beside you without a word, matching his pace to yours. After a while: "Morale is a resource, same as food or water. I've seen companies fall apart from a shortage of it before the enemy ever arrived."

choices.text: Ask what he did, in those companies, to hold things together.
Admit you don't have an easy answer for that.
Ask if he's worried about this company.

dain_d_ask_node.text: "Small things. Shared a meal. Told a bad joke. Reminded people why they started." He pauses. "It worked more often than it should have." He seems to be trying it now, in his own way.

dain_d_admit_node.text: "No one does, until it's tested," he says — not unkindly. "That's not a failure. It's just where we are."

dain_d_worried_node.text: He's quiet for a long moment. "Worried isn't the word. Watchful." He doesn't say more, but he doesn't need to.

dain_r_01.text: Dain studies the terrain as it changes, something almost like recognition in his expression. "I've walked this stretch before. Different company, different reasons. The road doesn't change much."

choices.text: Ask about the company he walked it with before.
Ask if he's glad to be walking it again.
Ask if anything's changed, then.

dain_r_company_node.text: "Soldiers. Most of them aren't anymore — discharged, or worse. I think about them when I pass through here. Hard not to."

dain_r_glad_node.text: He considers this longer than the question seems to warrant. "...Yes. I think I am." It sounds like it costs him something to admit.

dain_r_changed_node.text: "The road, no. What I notice now that I didn't then — that does." He doesn't elaborate, but he walks a little straighter for the rest of the stretch.

joe_ci_01.text: Joe falls into step beside you, already talking. "So I was thinking — the road forks up ahead, and I scouted both routes yesterday. Want the boring details or the short version?"

choices.text: The boring details, please.
Just the short version — surprise me.
Whichever route is faster.

joe_ci_boring_node.text: He launches into an enthusiastic, occasionally tangent-heavy breakdown of grade, footing, and one suspicious-looking bird he's pretty sure was watching him. You don't retain all of it, but his enthusiasm is infectious.

joe_ci_short_node.text: "Left fork's got a great view. Right fork's got a guy selling suspiciously good pies. That's the whole report." He looks very pleased with this summary.

joe_ci_fast_node.text: "Right fork, easy. Wanted an excuse to mention the pies though."

joe_b_01.text: Joe's already replaying the fight in his head, gesturing at the terrain where it happened. "Did you see how they tried to flank from the ridge? Same trick almost worked on a caravan I was with once."

choices.text: Ask what happened to that caravan.
Ask him to keep an eye out for the same trick in future.
Ask if he's secretly an expert on every kind of ambush.

joe_b_what_node.text: "Lost two wagons before someone finally spotted the second group. Lesson stuck, though — that's why I'm always checking the high ground now."

joe_b_watch_node.text: "Already on it," he says, with the satisfaction of someone whose job has just been validated. "Knew that habit would pay off eventually."

joe_b_expert_node.text: "Expert's a strong word. 'Survivor with good instincts' is more accurate. But I'll take expert."

joe_s_01.text: Joe squints up at the clearing sky with the air of someone reviewing his own work. "Saw that one coming, for what it's worth. Sky had that greenish look about an hour before. Should've said something."

choices.text: Ask him to explain the warning signs for next time.
Tell him not to worry about it — storms happen.
Ask if he has a 'feeling' about tomorrow's weather too.

joe_s_explain_node.text: He talks you through it — cloud color, wind shift, the particular quiet that settles over birds before a storm. It's oddly fascinating, and you find yourself watching the sky differently for the rest of the day.

joe_s_fine_node.text: "Appreciate that. Still gonna mention it next time, though. Old habit."

joe_s_feeling_node.text: He squints theatrically at the horizon. "...Feeling's saying 'probably fine.' Strong endorsement, I know."

joe_d_01.text: Joe's usual stream of chatter has thinned to almost nothing, which is somehow more noticeable than if he'd stopped talking entirely. After a while he says, quieter than usual, "Everyone's pretty tired, huh."

choices.text: Ask him to tell you something good — anything.
Agree, and ask if he's doing alright too.
Tell him his commentary is part of what's keeping people going.

joe_d_good_node.text: He thinks for a moment, then brightens — genuinely this time. "Okay — okay, I've got one." And he does have one, and it's better than you expected, and for a little while things feel lighter.

joe_d_agree_node.text: "Yeah. Mostly." He manages a small, real smile. "Thanks for asking, though. Means something."

joe_d_thanks_node.text: He looks startled, then genuinely pleased. "Yeah? Okay. Yeah, I can do that." And, true to form, he does.

joe_r_01.text: Joe's pace picks up noticeably as Kita comes into view in the distance. "There it is. Used to scout these roads for half the merchants coming through — feels strange seeing it from this side."

choices.text: Ask if he misses it.
Ask if he wants to stop in, even briefly.
Ask if Jenn still owes him money from whatever bet they had going.

joe_r_miss_node.text: "Sometimes. Mostly I miss knowing every street and every shortcut. Out here, I'm just guessing like everyone else." He doesn't seem too bothered by it.

joe_r_stop_node.text: He hesitates, clearly tempted, then shakes his head. "Better to keep moving. But — thanks for offering. Means something."

joe_r_jenn_node.text: He laughs. "She'll say I owe HER. We've been 'settling that bet' for two years. I think we both just like the excuse to argue about it."

jenn_ci_01.text: Jenn walks with her eyes half-closed, lips moving silently as she works through some internal verse, occasionally muttering a word and discarding it with a small shake of her head.

choices.text: Ask what she's working on.
Suggest a terrible rhyme, just to see her reaction.
Leave her to it — looks important.

jenn_ci_ask_node.text: "Something about the road. Or maybe about the people on it. Still arguing with myself over which." She doesn't stop muttering, but she smiles at you before returning to it.

jenn_ci_rhyme_node.text: She actually pauses, considers your terrible rhyme with theatrical horror, then bursts out laughing. "That's awful. I might use it."

jenn_ci_leave_node.text: She gives you a grateful nod, already half-gone again into whatever she's composing.

jenn_b_01.text: Jenn is already humming something under her breath, fitting words to a half-formed tune about the fight you just survived. "This one's got a good shape to it. Heroic, but not too neat. Those are my favorite."

choices.text: Ask to hear how it goes so far.
Ask her to make you sound more impressive than you actually were.
Ask what makes a story 'too neat.'

jenn_b_hear_node.text: She hums a few bars, voice low, just for you — rough, unfinished, but already carrying something of what just happened. It's strange, hearing your own fear and relief turned into music.

jenn_b_impress_node.text: "Oh, don't worry," she says, grinning. "By the third verse you'll have personally defeated twice as many of them. Artistic license."

jenn_b_neat_node.text: "When everything works out exactly as planned, with no cost. Nobody believes those, and nobody remembers them either."

jenn_s_01.text: Jenn is hoarse — she sang through most of the storm, an old call-and-response meant for exactly this kind of misery, and from the look of several others around camp, it helped more than anyone wants to admit.

choices.text: Thank her for keeping spirits up.
Ask where she learned that song.
Tell her she sounds like a drowned crow now.

jenn_s_thanks_node.text: "That's the job," she rasps, but she looks pleased — the kind of pleased that comes from doing something that actually mattered.

jenn_s_learn_node.text: "My grandmother. Sang it on washing day, of all things. Funny what sticks." She smiles, voice cracking slightly on the last word.

jenn_s_crow_node.text: She laughs, which turns into a cough, which turns into more laughing. "A drowned crow who KEPT EVERYONE WALKING, thank you very much."

jenn_d_01.text: Jenn doesn't hum today. She walks quietly, and when you catch her eye she gives a small, tired shrug. "Even I run out of songs, sometimes. Doesn't feel right, making something cheerful out of... this."

choices.text: Tell her it's alright not to perform today.
Ask if there's a quiet song instead of a cheerful one.
Offer to hum something terrible so she has something to react to.

jenn_d_ok_node.text: Something in her shoulders loosens. "...Thank you. I think I needed someone to say that." She walks beside you in comfortable silence for a while.

jenn_d_quiet_node.text: She thinks about it, then begins something low and slow — not cheerful, but not hopeless either. Just honest. It suits the moment better than anything upbeat would have.

jenn_d_terrible_node.text: She actually laughs — a real one. "That's... surprisingly close to working. Alright. Maybe I'm not completely out after all."

jenn_r_01.text: Jenn brightens as the road bends toward Kita. "Half my best material came from that town. Drunken arguments, terrible weddings, one truly legendary goat incident. I should write some of it down properly someday."

choices.text: Ask about the goat incident specifically.
Ask if she'll perform there again someday.
Suggest she write the goat one down right now, before she forgets.

jenn_r_goat_node.text: "Absolutely not. Some stories are better as legend than as fact. You'll just have to imagine the worst version and assume it's roughly accurate."

jenn_r_perform_node.text: "Maybe. Joe keeps saying I should. I think he just wants to hear the goat song again, honestly."

jenn_r_write_node.text: She actually pulls out a scrap of paper and starts scribbling, tongue between her teeth in concentration. "...You know, that's actually a good idea. Don't let me forget this."

scar_ci_01.text: Scarface walks a half-step behind you, eyes constantly moving — rooftops, treelines, anyone who looks twice. "You walk like someone who's never been robbed. I find that either impressive or concerning."

choices.text: Tell him you'd like to see someone try.
Ask what he's actually watching for.
Ask which one he's leaning toward — impressive or concerning.

scar_ci_dare_node.text: He gives a short, genuine laugh — rare for him. "There it is. Alright. Maybe you're not as soft as you look."

scar_ci_watching_node.text: "Anyone too interested in your pack. Anyone too interested in not being noticed. Same instinct, different angle." He doesn't stop scanning while he says it.

scar_ci_which_node.text: "Concerning. Definitely concerning." But there's no real edge to it — just Scarface being Scarface.

scar_b_01.text: Scarface checks the bodies with brisk efficiency — pockets, belts, anything worth taking — before you've even finished catching your breath. "Not bad. Could've been faster, but not bad."

choices.text: Ask what he'd have done differently.
Tell him you don't need the commentary.
Ask if 'not bad' is the highest praise he's capable of giving.

scar_b_ask_node.text: He actually answers, briskly but seriously — a couple of small, practical points about positioning. It's the closest thing to mentorship you've gotten from him.

scar_b_quiet_node.text: He raises both hands, mock-surrender, the ghost of a smirk on his face. "Fine, fine. Just an observation." He goes back to the pockets without further comment.

scar_b_praise_node.text: "From me? Yeah, pretty much. Don't let it go to your head." The almost-smile suggests he doesn't entirely mean that.

scar_s_01.text: Scarface barely seems to register the storm's aftermath, already wringing out his coat with the bored efficiency of someone who has done this many, many times before. "This is nothing. You should try sleeping in a drainage tunnel during the spring floods sometime."

choices.text: Ask what that was like.
Tell him that sounds like a personal problem.
Agree that it could be worse, and leave it at that.

scar_s_ask_node.text: His expression flickers — somewhere between memory and old habit of not talking about it. "Cold. Loud. Better than the alternative, most nights." He doesn't say what the alternative was, and you don't ask.

scar_s_personal_node.text: "It WAS a personal problem. Several, actually." He almost smiles, which for Scarface counts as an emotional breakthrough.

scar_s_agree_node.text: "Could always be worse," he agrees, and goes back to wringing out his coat like the conversation never happened.

scar_d_01.text: Scarface notices the mood before anyone says anything — he always does. He doesn't offer comfort, exactly. Instead: "Whatever's got everyone moping, it's not gonna fix itself by moping harder. Just so you know. Not that I care."

choices.text: Tell him that's oddly close to a kind thing to say.
Ask if he has a better suggestion, then.
Tell him to mind his own business.

scar_d_kind_node.text: "Don't push it," he mutters, but there's no real heat in it, and he doesn't walk away either — which, from Scarface, says more than the words do.

scar_d_suggest_node.text: "Find something to actually do. Standing around feeling bad just gives it more time to sink in." Blunt. Also, annoyingly, correct.

scar_d_mind_node.text: He shrugs, entirely unbothered. "Fine by me." But he doesn't leave, and neither does the observation, which lingers a bit longer than you'd like.

scar_r_01.text: Scarface goes quiet as the road nears Ualla, eyes flicking toward the town with something more wary than nostalgic. "Got some history here. Mostly the kind that involves people who'd be glad to see me again. For bad reasons."

choices.text: Ask if you should be worried.
Offer to handle it together if it comes to that.
Ask exactly how long the list of people is.

scar_r_worried_node.text: "Probably not. Probably." He doesn't sound entirely convinced, but he also doesn't slow down, so you take that as good enough.

scar_r_handle_node.text: He glances at you, surprised, then shrugs in a way that doesn't quite hide how much that landed. "...Yeah. Alright. Good to know."

scar_r_list_node.text: "Long enough that I stopped counting. Short enough that we'll probably be fine." Reassuring. Mostly.

lefty_ci_01.text: Lefty falls into step beside you, hands doing that idle thing they always do — testing the weight of pouches, counting coins by feel, pure habit at this point. "Relax. I'm not taking anything. Probably."

choices.text: Ask if 'probably' is supposed to be reassuring.
Tell him to keep his hands where you can see them.
Ask if he can ever actually turn it off.

lefty_ci_probably_node.text: "It's the best I've got," he admits, grinning. "Take it or leave it."

lefty_ci_hands_node.text: He holds both hands up, exaggeratedly visible, still grinning. "There. Happy?"

lefty_ci_offswitch_node.text: "Sometimes. On good days. This isn't one of those days, but don't worry — yours is safe. Mostly."

lefty_b_01.text: Lefty is already moving through the aftermath with practiced speed, pockets, packs, anything not nailed down. "Hey, credit where it's due — you all actually held the line back there. Made my job a lot easier."

choices.text: Tell him 'his job' isn't the only one that mattered.
Ask if that's his version of a thank-you.
Ask if he found anything good.

lefty_b_credit_node.text: He pauses, actually looks up from the loot for a second. "...Yeah. Yeah, fair. Wasn't trying to take anything away from that."

lefty_b_thanks_node.text: "Obviously. What, you want flowers too?" But he says it without any real bite.

lefty_b_loot_node.text: He holds up a small pouch with a satisfied grin. "Enough to make the day worthwhile. Don't ask too many questions about where it came from."

lefty_s_01.text: Lefty is in a foul mood, picking through a sodden pack with visible disgust. "Everything's wet. Everything. You know how hard it is to pick a lock with wet fingers? Nobody appreciates the technical difficulties of my profession."

choices.text: Tell him that sounds like a real hardship.
Suggest he dry his gear by the fire.
Ask how he got into this profession in the first place.

lefty_s_hardship_node.text: "It IS," he insists, completely serious, and somehow that makes it funnier.

lefty_s_dry_node.text: "Already on it," he grumbles, already arranging his things near the flames with surprising care for someone so careless about everything else.

lefty_s_history_node.text: His usual grin falters, just slightly. "Long story. Short version — when nobody's going to give you anything, you learn to take what you need. Anyway. Wet pockets, remember?" He goes back to his gear, conversation closed.

lefty_d_01.text: Lefty isn't his usual chatty self today — he walks with his hands in his pockets, quiet, until he finally says, almost to himself: "Used to be, I only looked out for me. Funny how that's not really true anymore."

choices.text: Tell him that's not a bad thing to have changed.
Ask what changed.
Tell him not to go soft on you now.

lefty_d_good_node.text: He looks at you sideways, like he's checking if you're mocking him. You're not. "...Yeah. Maybe not." He doesn't say much else, but he walks a little closer for the rest of the day.

lefty_d_changed_node.text: "Dunno, exactly. Just... started mattering, who made it through the day. Didn't used to." He shrugs, like the admission costs him something.

lefty_d_soft_node.text: "Wouldn't dream of it," he says, with a flicker of his old grin. "Just having a moment. I'll be insufferable again by tomorrow."

lefty_r_01.text: Lefty goes quiet as you near Yichesny, eyes scanning the skyline with something colder than his usual mischief. "Some people round here owe me. Or, well — I owe them, depending who you ask. Either way, there's history."

choices.text: Ask what kind of history.
Tell him you've got his back if it comes up.
Ask if 'the powerful' is code for someone specific.

lefty_r_history_node.text: "The kind where I had nothing, and they had everything, and they made very sure I'd stay that way." His voice is flat, all the usual humor gone. "Anyway. Old story."

lefty_r_back_node.text: He glances at you, and for once there's no joke ready. "...Thanks. Means something, that."

lefty_r_powerful_node.text: "Could be a lot of people, honestly. I was very thorough about making enemies here." The grin returns, but it doesn't quite reach his eyes.

velma_ci_01.text: Velma walks with her eyes on the horizon, and without any preamble: "Here's one for you — what walks the same road every day, yet never finds it the same twice?" She doesn't wait long for an answer.

choices.text: Guess: 'a river.'
Guess: 'a person who's changed.'
Admit you have no idea, and ask if there's a prize.

velma_ci_river_node.text: "Close. Rivers do that by nature. People have to choose to." She smiles faintly, the riddle apparently only half-answered.

velma_ci_person_node.text: She looks at you with something like approval. "Better than most answers I get. You've been paying attention."

velma_ci_noidea_node.text: "The prize is the question itself," she says serenely. "I know. Deeply unsatisfying. I get that a lot."

velma_b_01.text: Velma surveys the aftermath without triumph, expression unreadable. "A fight ends. The reasons for it rarely do. I wonder how many of these we'll need before someone asks why, instead of just how."

choices.text: Ask if she has an answer to that 'why.'
Say that today, at least, it kept people safe.
Tell her that's a question for another day.

velma_b_why_node.text: "Pieces of one. Enough to know it's bigger than any of us. Not enough to know what to do about it yet." She says it without despair — more like a scholar noting an unsolved problem.

velma_b_safe_node.text: "Today, yes," she agrees, and for once there's no riddle in it — just quiet acknowledgment.

velma_b_later_node.text: "Most are," she says, with something almost like a smile. "Doesn't stop me asking them anyway."

velma_s_01.text: Velma watches the clearing sky with unusual focus. "Everything changes after a storm — the ground, the river's path, what grows where. We rarely notice until much later. I wonder what's different now, that we won't see for a while yet."

choices.text: Ask if she means that literally or as a metaphor.
Say you hope whatever's different is for the better.
Tell her you were mostly just trying to stay dry.

velma_s_literal_node.text: "Both, usually. That's rather the point." She says it lightly, but there's real thought behind the words.

velma_s_hope_node.text: "So do I," she says, quietly, and for a moment the careful distance she usually keeps seems to soften.

velma_s_dry_node.text: She laughs — a rare, genuine sound. "A perfectly reasonable priority. The metaphors can wait until you're dry."

velma_d_01.text: Velma doesn't offer a riddle today — and somehow that's more unsettling than anything she might have said. When you ask if she's alright, she's quiet for a long moment. "I don't have an answer for this one. I don't like that I don't."

choices.text: Tell her she doesn't need to have all the answers.
Tell her that not knowing is sometimes the honest answer.
Ask what the question even was.

velma_d_noneed_node.text: She looks at you for a long moment, something unreadable crossing her face. "...No. I suppose I don't." It isn't relief, exactly, but it's close.

velma_d_honest_node.text: "Perhaps," she allows, slowly. "I'm not entirely comfortable with that kind of honesty. But perhaps."

velma_d_question_node.text: "Whether we're enough for what's coming." She shakes her head, almost to herself. "Not the kind of thing I can riddle my way around, it seems."

velma_r_01.text: Velma's pace slows as Yichesny comes into view, something almost wistful in her expression. "I spent years in the archives there. More books than people, most days. I learned a great deal. I'm not sure all of it was useful."

choices.text: Ask what she learned that wasn't useful.
Ask if she'd like to visit the archives again.
Ask if she misses the quiet.

velma_r_useless_node.text: "Mostly, that knowing things and being able to act on them are very different skills. The archives taught me the first. The road is teaching me the second."

velma_r_visit_node.text: She considers this, surprised by the offer. "...Perhaps. If there's time. Thank you for asking."
