velma_r_quiet_node.text: "Some days, terribly," she admits, with a small smile. "Other days, I remember how loud the silence could be, and I'm rather glad of the company."

ivan_ci_01.text: Ivan walks with the steady, unhurried pace of a man who has been paid by the day for a very long time. "Still on schedule. Still get paid either way. Just so we're clear on where we stand."

choices.text: Confirm that yes, the terms still stand.
Ask if he ever thinks about anything besides the contract.
Ask what he'd do if the pay stopped.

ivan_ci_confirm_node.text: "Good." That's it. That's the whole response. He keeps walking, apparently satisfied.

ivan_ci_else_node.text: He actually considers this, like it's a more interesting question than he expected. "Sometimes. Usually about food. Good food's worth almost as much as the coin."

ivan_ci_stopped_node.text: "Then I'd have a different conversation with whoever stopped paying it." He says it without menace — just fact. "Hasn't come up yet, though."

ivan_b_01.text: Ivan wipes down his weapon with brisk, practiced motions, already running through the fight in his head. "Sloppy in places. Nobody died, though, so. Acceptable."

choices.text: Ask what was sloppy, specifically.
Tell him 'acceptable' might be the nicest thing he's said.
Agree — nobody died, that's what matters.

ivan_b_sloppy_node.text: He gives you an actual rundown — short, clipped, but genuinely useful, the kind of feedback that comes from someone who's survived a lot of fights by paying attention to exactly this.

ivan_b_nicest_node.text: "Don't get used to it," he says, but there's the faintest twitch at the corner of his mouth that might, charitably, be called a smile.

ivan_b_alive_node.text: "That's what matters," he agrees, sheathing his weapon. "Everything else is just notes for next time."

ivan_s_01.text: Ivan barely breaks stride through the storm's aftermath, mud and all, like it's simply part of the day's work. "Worked three winters on the Kell border. This is a light drizzle by comparison."

choices.text: Ask about the Kell border.
Ask if anything actually fazes him.
Agree it could be worse and move on.

ivan_s_kell_node.text: "Cold enough to crack steel. Contracts up there paid well for a reason." He doesn't elaborate further, but there's a flicker of something — old memory, maybe — before his expression settles back to neutral.

ivan_s_fazes_node.text: He actually pauses to consider this, seriously. "Running out of arrows. That's about it."

ivan_s_worse_node.text: "Could be worse," he agrees, and that's the end of the conversation, as far as he's concerned.

ivan_d_01.text: Ivan doesn't usually have much to say about morale — that's not his department, as far as he's concerned. But today, watching the others trudge along in silence, something in his usual flat expression shifts. "...Hard, this. Harder than the fighting, some days."

choices.text: Ask if he's alright too.
Agree, and leave it at that.
Tell him that's the most human thing you've ever heard him say.

ivan_d_alright_node.text: He's quiet for a moment. "...Fine. Just an observation." But he doesn't walk away immediately, and that, for Ivan, says plenty.

ivan_d_agree_node.text: He nods once, like that settles something, and the two of you walk on without further words. Sometimes that's enough.

ivan_d_human_node.text: "Don't get used to it," he mutters, and the brief crack in his composure seals back over — but not quite as completely as before.

ivan_r_01.text: Ivan slows slightly as the road nears Shishy's Tavern, eyes scanning the building with something like recognition. "Picked up this job there. Good ale, better information. Half my contracts start in places like that."

choices.text: Ask what kind of information you can get at a place like that.
Ask if he ever regrets taking this particular job.
Ask if the ale's really that good.

ivan_r_info_node.text: "Who's hiring, who's hiding, who's about to be neither." He says it like a simple statement of fact, which, to him, it is.

ivan_r_regret_node.text: He's quiet for a moment, actually thinking about it. "No," he says finally. "Strange, given how it started. But no."

ivan_r_ale_node.text: "It's ale," he says, with the air of a man who has had much worse and is therefore satisfied with merely adequate.

ick_ci_01.text: Ick is arranging small stones in a careful spiral near the camp, pausing every so often to consider his work with what looks disturbingly like deliberation, before adjusting one stone by what cannot be more than a hair's width.

choices.text: Watch and try to figure out the pattern.
Add a stone of your own and see what happens.
Leave him to it — probably best not to disturb whatever this is.

ick_ci_watch_node.text: The longer you watch, the less random it seems — and the more you start to wonder if that's a comforting thought or not. Ick glances up at you, and for just a moment, you'd swear he knows exactly what you're thinking.

ick_ci_addstone_node.text: Ick studies your stone for a long moment, then very deliberately moves it to what is, you have to admit, a much better spot. He looks almost smug about it.

ick_ci_leave_node.text: Ick doesn't look up, but his tail gives a single approving flick, as though grading your judgment and finding it acceptable.

ick_b_01.text: While everyone else catches their breath, Ick sits very still, staring at the fallen enemies with an expression that — on a person — you'd call thoughtful. It lasts a beat too long to be comfortable.

choices.text: Watch to see what he does next.
Nudge him gently, just to break the moment.
Joke that he's planning something.

ick_b_watch_node.text: Eventually Ick simply turns away and trots back toward you, tail held normally again, as if nothing happened at all. You're left with the distinct, uncomfortable feeling that something passed between him and the moment that you weren't meant to understand.

ick_b_nudge_node.text: Ick blinks, shakes himself once, and is suddenly, completely himself again — scurrying over for attention like any ordinary rat. The change is almost too immediate.

ick_b_joke_node.text: Ick looks up at you, and you could swear — just for a second — there's something amused in those small dark eyes. Then he's just a rat again, sniffing at your boots.

ick_s_01.text: While the rest of camp shivers and grumbles through the storm's aftermath, Ick burrows contentedly into the folds of your pack, apparently unbothered, occasionally peering out with what looks almost like sympathy for everyone else's suffering.

choices.text: Ask him to share whatever secret he knows about staying warm.
Wonder, not for the first time, what exactly he is.
Be glad, at least, that someone's comfortable.

ick_s_share_node.text: Ick says nothing, obviously, but he does shuffle over very slightly to share the warmest spot in the pack — which feels like answer enough.

ick_s_what_node.text: Not for the first time, you get no answer — just a small, dark-eyed look that seems to say the question is the wrong one to be asking. You let it go, as you always do.

ick_s_glad_node.text: Ick peeks out at you, and — you could swear — does something that looks remarkably like a shrug, before burrowing back down. Somehow it's reassuring.

ick_d_01.text: As the mood around camp turns heavy, Ick climbs, unprompted, onto your shoulder, and simply stays there — a small, warm, oddly steadying weight that doesn't ask anything of you at all.

choices.text: Let him stay, and feel a little steadier for it.
Wonder how he always seems to know.
Thank him formally, like he's a tiny, furry counselor.

ick_d_let_node.text: He stays there for a long while, through the worst of it, and somehow that's exactly enough.

ick_d_how_node.text: You don't get an answer, of course — just that same knowing stillness. But you've stopped being surprised by it, and started, in a strange way, being grateful for it.

ick_d_thanks_node.text: Ick tilts his head at you, entirely unbothered by the absurdity, and stays exactly where he is. Apparently the appointment stands.

ick_r_01.text: As the Glittering Gate looms into view, Ick goes utterly still on your shoulder — more still than you've ever seen him — staring at the structure with an intensity that raises the hair on your arms.

choices.text: Ask, quietly, if he recognizes this place.
Stay close to him, just in case.
Tell him it's just a gate, nothing to be dramatic about.

ick_r_recognize_node.text: He doesn't answer, of course. But the stillness lasts until the Gate is well behind you, and only then does he relax, shaking himself out as if shedding something unseen.

ick_r_close_node.text: He presses closer against you, and for once, you don't get the sense he's entirely unbothered. Whatever this place means to him, he doesn't want to face it alone.

ick_r_dramatic_node.text: Ick does not dignify this with any reaction whatsoever, which — given everything else about him — feels like a reaction in itself.

glub_ci_01.text: Glubglub bounces along beside you, talking mostly to himself. "Glubglub thinks today is a good day for walking! Very good road. Very... very roadly. Is that a word? Glubglub thinks it should be."

choices.text: Tell him 'roadly' is definitely a word now.
Ask what makes a road 'roadly.'
Agree it's a good day for walking.

glub_ci_word_node.text: "Glubglub knew it! Glubglub is very good with words. Mostly."

glub_ci_what_node.text: He thinks hard, tongue poking out the side of his mouth. "...Glubglub doesn't know. But this road has it. Other roads, maybe not so much." He nods firmly, as if this settles the matter.

glub_ci_agree_node.text: "Yes! Yes, exactly!" He practically vibrates with agreement, delighted that someone understands his very important point.

glub_b_01.text: Glubglub is reenacting the battle with enthusiastic, wildly inaccurate gestures. "And THEN Glubglub jumped — like THIS — and hit FIVE of them! Maybe six! It was very impressing!"

choices.text: Ask if it was really six.
Tell him you definitely remember it that way too.
Gently note that you don't remember six.

glub_b_six_node.text: "...Maybe two," Glubglub admits, slightly deflating, before perking right back up. "But they were BIG twos!"

glub_b_remember_node.text: Glubglub's whole face lights up. "You SAW it?! Glubglub knew someone saw it!" He looks ready to burst with pride.

glub_b_note_node.text: "Glubglub remembers it different," he says, completely unbothered, already moving on to recounting it a third, even more dramatic way.

glub_s_01.text: Glubglub is thoroughly soaked and thoroughly unhappy about it, muttering to himself. "No silver cloud. No silver cloud AT ALL. Just wet. Very wet. Glubglub does not approve of this lining."

choices.text: Gently correct him — it's 'silver lining.'
Offer him a dry cloak from your pack.
Tell him you don't approve of it either, for solidarity.

glub_s_correct_node.text: "That is what Glubglub said," he insists, completely unconvinced, water dripping steadily off his nose.

glub_s_cloak_node.text: Glubglub's whole demeanor brightens immediately. "Glubglub accepts! Glubglub accepts very much!" He wraps himself in it like a tiny, soggy burrito.

glub_s_solidarity_node.text: Glubglub looks genuinely touched. "Glubglub is glad someone else also does not approve. Makes the not-approving feel more... official."

glub_d_01.text: Glubglub isn't talking to himself today, which is somehow more worrying than anything he could have said. When you check on him, he just shrugs, small and uncharacteristically subdued. "Glubglub doesn't know how to make this part better. Glubglub is sorry."

choices.text: Tell him it's not his job to fix it, and that's okay.
Ask for one of his terrible jokes anyway.
Tell him just walking with everyone helps more than he thinks.

glub_d_notjob_node.text: Glubglub looks up at you, eyes a little too bright. "...Okay," he says, quietly, and for once doesn't have anything else to add. He stays close for the rest of the walk.

glub_d_joke_node.text: He thinks hard, then offers, very seriously: "Why did the chicken... Glubglub forgets the rest. But it was funny!" Somehow, that's exactly the right amount of terrible.

glub_d_walking_node.text: Glubglub considers this for a long moment, then nods slowly, looking a little less small. "...Okay. Glubglub can do that."

glub_r_01.text: As the road climbs toward Colrandrir, Glubglub gets noticeably twitchy — equal parts excited and nervous, talking faster than usual. "Glubglub knows this place! Glubglub grew up around here! Maybe. Some of here. The down parts, mostly."

choices.text: Ask what it was like growing up here.
Tell him you're glad he's showing you around.
Ask what 'the down parts' means exactly.

glub_r_growup_node.text: His enthusiasm dims, just slightly. "Cold. And big. Everything was very big, when Glubglub was little. Still is, really." He looks up at the cliffs, and for a moment seems smaller than usual.

glub_r_guide_node.text: Glubglub puffs up with pride immediately, all nerves forgotten. "Glubglub is an excellent guide! The BEST guide! Probably!"

glub_r_downparts_node.text: "The parts that are down," Glubglub explains, with the patient tone of someone explaining something very obvious. "As opposed to the up parts. Those are scarier."

mira_ci_01.text: You don't hear Mira approach — you never do. She's just suddenly there, at the edge of your vision, watching the road ahead with quiet focus. "Clear for now," she says, by way of greeting.

choices.text: Ask if she ever relaxes.
Ask what she's looking for, exactly.
Thank her for keeping watch.

mira_ci_relax_node.text: "When it's clear," she says. It takes you a moment to realize that, by her own definition, this is her relaxing.

mira_ci_lookfor_node.text: "Anything that doesn't belong. Usually it's nothing. The times it isn't nothing are why I keep looking."

mira_ci_thanks_node.text: She gives you the smallest possible nod — barely a movement at all — but you get the sense it means more than it looks like.

mira_b_01.text: Mira is already wiping down her blades, expression unreadable as she reviews the fight in her head. "Efficient. Almost too efficient." She doesn't elaborate immediately.

choices.text: Ask what 'too efficient' means.
Tell her efficient is exactly what you needed.
Ask if she's complaining about winning too easily.

mira_b_efficient_node.text: She's quiet for a moment. "Means I didn't have to think. Just... reacted. That's useful. It's also how people stop noticing what they've become." She sheathes her blades and says nothing further.

mira_b_needed_node.text: "Good," she says simply, and the corner of her mouth moves in something that might, on anyone else, be called a smile.

mira_b_complaining_node.text: She gives you a long, flat look that suggests she has heard this joke before and was not amused the first time either. But there's no real annoyance behind it.

mira_s_01.text: While everyone else huddles miserably against the rain, Mira has already found the best cover available — a rock overhang most people would have walked right past. "Storms are useful. Nobody's watching the road in weather like this."

choices.text: Ask how she always finds spots like this.
Tell her that's a very practical way to look at being soaked.
Settle in next to her and say nothing — just keep her company.

mira_s_findspots_node.text: "Practice. And paying attention to where I'd hide, if I needed to." She says it so matter-of-factly that you're not sure if it's reassuring or slightly unsettling.

mira_s_settle_node.text: She glances at you, surprised, then says nothing — but she doesn't move away either, and the silence between you feels easier than most conversations.

mira_d_01.text: Mira is harder to find than usual today — even for her. When you do find her, she's sitting alone, just watching the road. She doesn't look up. "Sometimes I forget what we're walking toward. Just... the walking. Is that bad?"

choices.text: Tell her it's alright to just focus on the walking sometimes.
Ask what she pictures, when she does remember.
Tell her that's probably how most people get through it.

mira_d_alright_node.text: She's quiet for a long moment. "...Okay." It's barely a word, but something in her posture eases, just slightly, and she lets you sit there with her a while longer than usual.

mira_d_picture_node.text: "Nothing good," she says quietly, and doesn't elaborate. But she doesn't pull away when you stay either.

mira_d_mostpeople_node.text: She considers this, then gives the smallest nod. "...Maybe. That's something, at least."

mira_r_01.text: As the road grows rougher and the shadows longer, Mira seems, if anything, more at ease — moving with quiet familiarity through terrain that makes everyone else nervous. "I know this kind of ground. Spent a long time in places like this. Longer than I'd like to admit."

choices.text: Ask what kind of places, exactly.
Tell her you're glad to have someone who knows this ground.
Ask if she has any tips for looking that unbothered.

mira_r_whatplaces_node.text: "The kind most people try not to think about." Her tone doesn't invite follow-up, and you don't push — but she doesn't seem upset that you asked, either.

mira_r_glad_node.text: She glances at you, something unreadable in her expression. "...Yeah. Glad to be useful for it." It's as close to warmth as she gets.

mira_r_tips_node.text: "Stop expecting things to go wrong, and they will anyway. Expect it, and sometimes you're pleasantly surprised." She says it completely deadpan, and you can't tell if she's joking.

okuna_r_01.text: The Dockside Trader leans against a crate, watching the road inland with a frown. "Been hearing odd things from travelers coming down that way. Talk of the war creeping closer than the maps say it should. Just... watch yourself out there."

choices.text: Ask what kind of 'odd things.'
Thank him for the warning and move on.
Ask if he's just trying to upsell you on supplies.

okuna_r_what_node.text: "Hard to say, exactly. Soldiers moving the wrong direction. Refugees moving faster than they should. Things that don't add up, if you're paying attention." He shrugs, like he's said more than he meant to.

okuna_r_thanks_node.text: "Mm. Stay sharp, that's all," he says, already turning back to his crates.

okuna_r_upsell_node.text: He barks a short laugh. "Caught me. Mostly. But the warning's real too. Believe what you like."

okuna_p_01.text: The Dockside Trader's eyes light up with recognition as you approach. "Heard your name 'round the docks, you know. Good things, mostly. Folk like that, I keep the good stuff where they can actually find it."

choices.text: Thank him for the kind words.
Ask what 'the good stuff' is.
Ask what 'mostly' is doing in that sentence.

okuna_p_thanks_node.text: He waves it off, looking pleased anyway. "Just saying what I hear. Stock's a bit better today, if you're looking."

okuna_p_goodstuff_node.text: He gestures vaguely toward a crate that looks identical to the others, and slides a few coins back across the counter. "Things I don't put out for just anybody. You'll know it when you see it."

okuna_p_mostly_node.text: "Mostly," he repeats, with a wink, and says nothing further — which is somehow more concerning than reassuring.

okuna_g_01.text: The Dockside Trader looks up from sorting crates, giving you an appraising once-over. "Help you find something? Got the basics, little extra besides, if you know where to look. Which, lucky for you, is right here."

choices.text: Ask what's selling well lately.
Tell him you're just browsing — for now.
Ask how long he's run this place.

okuna_g_selling_node.text: "Rations, mostly. Folk heading inland buy up everything that doesn't spoil. Smart, really." He nods toward his shelves.

okuna_g_browsing_node.text: "Take your time," he says, already losing interest, going back to his crates.

okuna_g_howlong_node.text: "Long enough to know most faces that come through here. Yours is new. We'll see if it sticks around."

amrik_r_01.text: The Village Merchant lowers her voice as she wraps your purchase. "More soldiers passing through than usual lately. Nobody says much, but you can tell things are... moving. Whatever's coming, it's coming faster than folks expected."

choices.text: Ask if she's worried.
Ask if there's anything useful she's heard specifically.
Tell her you intend to do something about it.

amrik_r_worried_node.text: "Always am, a little. But worry doesn't stock shelves, does it?" She manages a tired smile and keeps wrapping.

amrik_r_useful_node.text: "Not really — mostly just nerves and rumor. But when this many people get nervous at once, it's usually for a reason."

amrik_r_doSomething_node.text: She pauses, looking at you properly for the first time. "...Well. Good. Somebody should." She seems to mean it.

amrik_p_01.text: The Village Merchant's expression brightens as she recognizes you. "Oh — it's you! We've heard a bit about what you've been up to. Here, let me see what I can do about that price for you."

choices.text: Thank her, a little embarrassed by the attention.
Ask exactly what she's heard.
Accept the discount gratefully and move on.

amrik_p_thanks_node.text: "Don't be shy about it," she says warmly. "Good news is rare enough out here. Let people enjoy it."

amrik_p_heard_node.text: She grins. "Enough to know you're worth being nice to. That's really all that matters to a shopkeeper."

amrik_p_accept_node.text: "Of course," she says, already adjusting the price with practiced ease. "Least I can do."

amrik_g_01.text: The Village Merchant greets you with the easy warmth of someone who's spent years getting to know everyone who passes through. "Welcome, welcome! Let me know if you need help finding anything."

choices.text: Ask what's been popular with other travelers.
Ask if she's heard any interesting news lately.
Tell her you're mostly here to admire the shelves.

amrik_g_popular_node.text: "Healing potions, mostly, and warm cloaks once the nights start getting colder. Practical types, travelers."

amrik_g_news_node.text: "This and that. Mostly the same rumors everyone else is passing around. Nothing I'd bet coin on."

amrik_g_shelves_node.text: She laughs warmly. "Well, they are very nice shelves. I dust them myself."

kanlin_r_01.text: Kanlin glances toward the door before speaking, voice lowered. "Been seeing rougher sorts coming through the waystation lately. Deserters, mostly, I think. Keep an eye on your things if you're stopping for the night."

choices.text: Thank him for the heads-up.
Ask if he's had any trouble himself.
Offer to keep an eye out for trouble while you're here.

kanlin_r_thanks_node.text: "Just looking out for paying customers," he says, with a small nod, already moving on to the next task.

kanlin_r_trouble_node.text: "Nothing I couldn't handle. But it adds up, you know? Wears on a place, having to watch the door all the time."

kanlin_r_offer_node.text: He looks genuinely relieved. "That'd... actually help, honestly. Appreciated."

kanlin_p_01.text: Kanlin's friendly demeanor cools noticeably as he recognizes you. "...Heard a few things about you, traveler. Nothing official, mind. Just— let's keep this quick and simple, yeah?"

choices.text: Tell him you're not here to cause trouble.
Agree — quick and simple works fine.
Ask exactly what he's heard, out of curiosity.

kanlin_p_notrouble_node.text: He holds up both hands, stepping back slightly. "Didn't say you were! Just— being careful. No offense meant." He relaxes, marginally.

kanlin_p_agree_node.text: "Good," he says, visibly relieved, and gets through the transaction with brisk efficiency.

kanlin_p_heard_node.text: "Things I'd rather not repeat to your face," he says, with a thin smile that doesn't reach his eyes. "Let's just leave it there."

kanlin_g_01.text: Kanlin looks up from restocking shelves, offering a businesslike nod. "Waystation's open. Take what you need — just don't dawdle too long, got a line forming behind you most days."

choices.text: Ask what sells fastest here.
Ask how busy the waystation usually gets.
Tell him you'll try not to take it personally.

kanlin_g_fastest_node.text: "Rations and healing potions, same as everywhere. Travelers don't get creative with their priorities, generally."

kanlin_g_busy_node.text: "Depends on the season. Right now? Busier than I'd like. Good for business, bad for my feet."

kanlin_g_personal_node.text: He snorts, almost a laugh. "Wasn't personal. Mostly."

lahonis_r_01.text: The market vendor counting your coins pauses, glancing south along the road. "Funny thing — used to get news from the south every week, regular as anything. Lately it's slowed to almost nothing. Either nothing's happening down there, or..."

choices.text: Ask what the alternative is.
Suggest maybe it's just bad luck with messengers.
Say you'll find out, one way or another.

lahonis_r_alt_node.text: "...Or something's stopping the news from getting through. I'd rather it was the first one, honestly. But I wouldn't bet on it."

lahonis_r_luck_node.text: "Maybe," the vendor allows, though they don't sound convinced. "Let's hope that's all it is."

lahonis_r_findout_node.text: The vendor looks at you for a long moment, then nods slowly. "...Yeah. Maybe you will, at that."

lahonis_p_01.text: Word seems to travel fast through the Lahonis Market — several vendors nod respectfully as you pass, and the one helping you leans in with a grin. "You're the one folks have been talking about, aren't you? Here — let me show you what we keep for, ah, valued customers."

choices.text: Ask what makes a customer 'valued.'
Play along and ask to see the good stuff.
Just thank them and continue browsing normally.

lahonis_p_what_node.text: "Reputation, mostly. And good manners. You've got both, from what I hear — and what I've seen just now." They seem genuinely pleased to say it.

lahonis_p_play_node.text: They produce a small, neatly wrapped selection of goods from beneath the counter with a flourish. "Ta-da. Don't tell the others."

lahonis_p_normal_node.text: "Suit yourself," they say, easygoing about it, though they leave the offer open with a knowing look.

lahonis_g_01.text: The Lahonis Market is loud and crowded as always, vendors calling out over each other. The one nearest you waves you over with a grin. "Best prices on this side of the square, guaranteed! Well — guaranteed by me, anyway."

choices.text: Ask how much that guarantee is actually worth.
Ask what's worth buying here specifically.
Ask how long the market's been here.

lahonis_g_worth_node.text: "Absolutely nothing, officially," they admit cheerfully. "But I stand by it anyway. Good faith and all that."

lahonis_g_buy_node.text: "Honestly? Whatever you can carry. We get a bit of everything through here — better selection than most places you'll find on the road."

lahonis_g_history_node.text: "Generations, they say. My grandmother sold here, and hers before that. Lahonis has always been a crossroads."

zilam_r_01.text: The Zilam Outfitters' owner glances over a shipping manifest with a furrowed brow. "Orders for gear are up. Way up. Somebody's preparing for something — and it's not the kind of preparing that ends quietly."

choices.text: Ask who's placing the orders.
Ask if that means prices are going up too.
Ask if there's anything you should know before heading further.

zilam_r_who_node.text: "Officially? Couldn't say. Unofficially?" They lower their voice. "Military types, mostly. Lot of them."

zilam_r_prices_node.text: "Afraid so. Demand does that. Lucky for you, I like you enough to hold the line a bit longer than I should."

zilam_r_know_node.text: They consider this seriously. "Mostly — be ready. Whatever's building, it's building toward something. Better to have the gear and not need it."

zilam_p_01.text: The Zilam Outfitters' owner looks you over with the practiced eye of someone who's outfitted a lot of soldiers. "You carry yourself like someone who's actually been through it. Heard the stories too, for what it's worth. Let's get you properly equipped."

choices.text: Thank them for the consideration.
Ask what 'properly equipped' means in practice.
Ask if you get a discount for looking the part.

zilam_p_thanks_node.text: "Don't thank me yet," they say, with a faint smile. "Thank me if it actually helps out there."

zilam_p_meaning_node.text: "Means matching gear to what you're actually facing, not just what looks impressive on a shelf. I've got opinions. Strong ones."

zilam_p_discount_node.text: "For looking the part AND being the part? Sure, why not." They wave off your protest before you can make one.

zilam_g_01.text: The Zilam Outfitters is all business — racks of armor and weapons arranged with military precision. The owner nods at you without looking up from a ledger. "Take a look around. Everything's labeled. Mostly accurately."

choices.text: Ask what's recommended for the road ahead.
Ask what 'mostly accurately' covers.
Ask if they served, before this.

zilam_g_recommend_node.text: "Depends where you're headed and what you're expecting to fight. Come find me if you want specifics — I've got opinions for days."

zilam_g_mostly_node.text: Finally they look up, with the ghost of a smile. "One mislabeled crate, years ago. I've never lived it down. Vow of total accuracy ever since."

zilam_g_served_node.text: "Long enough ago that it doesn't matter much anymore," they say, in a tone that closes the subject without being unfriendly about it.

sdrakam_r_01.text: The Sdrakam Armory's smith doesn't look up from the forge as you enter. "Had someone through here last week. Wouldn't say much, but they'd clearly been in a fight with something big. Real big. Wouldn't say what, either."

choices.text: Ask if they're alright now.
Ask if the smith has any theories.
Say you'll be careful.

sdrakam_r_alright_node.text: "Walking, last I saw. Wouldn't call it 'alright.'" The smith finally glances up. "Whatever it was, it left a mark."

sdrakam_r_theories_node.text: The smith shrugs, hammer never quite stopping. "Got theories. None I like. Won't waste your time with them."

sdrakam_r_careful_node.text: The smith pauses, actually meeting your eyes for the first time. "...Good. Do that." Then back to the forge.

sdrakam_p_01.text: The Sdrakam Armory's smith eyes you with open suspicion as you approach. "Heard your name before. Heard it in ways that make me want to see coin up front, if it's all the same to you."

choices.text: Ask if that's really necessary.
Agree — coin up front is fine.
Ask what exactly they heard, out of curiosity.

sdrakam_p_necessary_node.text: The smith doesn't flinch, but doesn't back down either. "For you? Yeah. Necessary." The hammer doesn't stop, but the message is clear.

sdrakam_p_agree_node.text: "Appreciated," the smith says, somewhat surprised by the lack of argument, and the transaction proceeds without further comment.

sdrakam_p_curious_node.text: "Things I choose not to repeat while you're standing in my shop," the smith says flatly, and goes back to the forge.

sdrakam_g_01.text: The Sdrakam Armory rings with the steady clang of hammer on steel. The smith barely glances up. "Browse if you want. Ask if you need. Don't touch the stuff still glowing."

choices.text: Promise not to touch the glowing stuff.
Ask what's fresh off the forge.
Ask how long they've been smithing.

sdrakam_g_promise_node.text: "Wise," the smith says, without a trace of humor, though something in their shoulders relaxes slightly.

sdrakam_g_fresh_node.text: The smith gestures with the hammer toward a rack near the back. "That lot, this morning. Still settling. Good work, if I do say so."

sdrakam_g_howlong_node.text: "Since I was younger than I'd like to admit. Forge doesn't care how old you are, as long as the work's good."

kita_r_01.text: The Kita Emporium's keeper sighs, glancing out at the street. "Used to be Kita stayed out of all this. Lately, though — even here, people are starting to talk like the war's not 'somewhere else' anymore."

choices.text: Ask what people are saying, specifically.
Ask if the shop's been affected.
Say that's exactly why you're out here.

kita_r_saying_node.text: "Mostly just worry, dressed up as gossip. But worry like that doesn't usually come from nothing."

kita_r_affected_node.text: "A bit. Some goods are harder to get than they used to be. Nothing dire yet. 'Yet' being the word that worries me."

kita_r_whyOut_node.text: The keeper looks at you for a moment, then nods slowly. "...Good. I hope that's enough. I really do."

kita_p_01.text: The Kita Emporium's keeper brightens as you enter. "Ah — so you're the one! Word's made it even out here. Joe mentioned someone matching your description, actually. Said good things, for what that's worth."

choices.text: Ask how Joe's doing.
Ask what exactly Joe said.
Thank them and ask about today's stock.

kita_p_joe_node.text: "Same as ever — in and out, never quite where you expect. But fond of you, clearly. That's rare, from him."

kita_p_said_node.text: "Something like 'don't sell them the cursed dagger, they don't deserve that.' High praise, from Joe."

kita_p_stock_node.text: "Of course! And let me say — for someone with your reputation, I think we can do a little better on price today."

kita_g_01.text: The Kita Emporium is a delightful clutter of shelves, each one a different kind of chaos. The keeper smiles warmly. "Welcome! Fair warning — the organization system makes sense to exactly one person, and that's me. Ask if you're lost."

choices.text: Admit you're already lost.
Ask what's actually worth buying here.
Ask about the strange items on the high shelf.

kita_g_lost_node.text: "Wonderful! Everyone is, the first time. Here, let me walk you through it — it really does make sense, I promise."

kita_g_buy_node.text: "Depends what you need! But the potions are reliable, and I don't sell anything I wouldn't use myself. Mostly."

kita_g_shelf_node.text: "Oh, those? Some of those have been up there longer than I've owned the shop. I keep meaning to find out what they actually do."

nabis_r_01.text: The Nabis Vaults' keeper speaks in a low, careful voice, as though the walls themselves might be listening. "Past here, the roads get... unreliable. Some call it the Blasted Lands. Most who go in with plans come out with different ones. If they come out at all."

choices.text: Ask if there's any way to prepare for what's ahead.
Ask what they mean by 'different plans.'
Ask if there's a safer route around.

nabis_r_prepare_node.text: The keeper studies you for a long moment, then turns toward a locked case behind the counter. "...Maybe. Let's see what we have that might actually help."

nabis_r_different_node.text: "The land changes people, out there. Not always for the worse. But always." They don't elaborate further, and you don't ask them to.

nabis_r_safer_node.text: "There's always a way around," the keeper says slowly, "but 'around' tends to take you somewhere else just as bad. Sometimes worse."

nabis_p_01.text: The Nabis Vaults' keeper studies you with unusual intensity, then, seemingly satisfied by what they see, moves toward a heavily locked case in the back. "We don't show this to most people. But most people haven't done what you have, either."

choices.text: Ask what's in the case.
Ask how they know what you've done.
Wait quietly to see what they bring out.

nabis_p_whatsin_node.text: The keeper unlocks it carefully, revealing a small selection of items that practically hum with quality — clearly the best the vault has to offer. "Consider it... recognition. Use it well."

nabis_p_how_node.text: "Word travels strangely, this close to the edge of things. People remember names, out here. Especially names attached to good outcomes."

nabis_p_wait_node.text: The keeper returns with a small selection of items set carefully on a velvet cloth — clearly not the usual stock, and clearly meant as a quiet gesture of respect.

nabis_g_01.text: The Nabis Vaults are quiet, dim, and orderly — a sharp contrast to the wilder country beyond. The keeper inclines their head politely. "Welcome. We deal mostly in things travelers don't realize they need until they very much do."

choices.text: Ask what's recommended for travelers headed further out.
Ask how the vaults came to be all the way out here.
Ask for an example of something you 'don't realize you need.'

nabis_g_recommend_node.text: "Anything that keeps you alive in places where help isn't coming. I'd start there, if I were you."

nabis_g_howcame_node.text: "Someone, long ago, decided the edge of the known world needed a well-stocked shop. Whether that was wisdom or madness depends who you ask."

nabis_g_example_node.text: The keeper produces a small, plain stone and sets it on the counter. "This, for example. Most people laugh. Most people who laughed are not here to laugh about it twice."
